title: A zero-image germ from a finitely presented module is killed by a finitely presented quotient
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] which is quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme] and quasi-separated [def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism]. Let $\mathcal G,\mathcal F$ be sheaves of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], with $\mathcal G$ of finite presentation [def-weil-pbc-module-finite-type-presentation] and $\mathcal F$ quasi-coherent [pqf-def-coherent], and let $\alpha:\mathcal G\to\mathcal F$ be $\mathcal O_X$-linear. Let $x\in X$ and let $s\in\mathcal G_x$ be a germ in the ordinary Zariski module stalk [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk] with $\alpha_x(s)=0$. Then there is a quasi-coherent submodule $\mathcal K\subseteq\mathcal G$ of finite type [def-weil-pbc-module-finite-type-presentation], contained in the sectionwise kernel $\ker\alpha$ (so $\alpha_U(\mathcal K(U))=0$ for every open $U\subseteq X$), such that the quotient $\mathcal Q=\mathcal G/\mathcal K$, the cokernel in $\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O_X)$ of $\mathcal K\hookrightarrow\mathcal G$, is of finite presentation, and its quotient map $q:\mathcal G\to\mathcal Q$ satisfies $q_x(s)=0$. Moreover there is an $\mathcal O_X$-linear map $\beta:\mathcal Q\to\mathcal F$ with $\beta\circ q=\alpha$.

source.place: Stacks Properties, Lemma 01PJ (lemma-directed-colimit-diagram-finite-presentation), injectivity paragraph, lines 3137-3163: finite-type quasi-coherent submodule inside the kernel, and finite-presentation quotient killing the chosen germ.

proof.text: Represent $s$ by a section $t$ near $x$. The germ equality criterion shrinks its domain to $W$ where the image under $\alpha$ vanishes. Choose an affine open neighbourhood $x\in U\subseteq W$ using the scheme affine-open basis, and restrict $t$ to $U$. An affine open is quasi-compact, its image section is zero, and its germ remains $s$.

Finite presentation makes $\mathcal G$ quasi-coherent by the finite-presentation instance in Mathlib. Since $\mathcal F$ is quasi-coherent, the kernel theorem gives the quasi-coherent sheaf $\mathcal H=\ker\alpha$, with $\mathcal H(T)=\ker\alpha_T$ for every open $T$. In particular $t\in\mathcal H(U)$.

Regard the section of $\mathcal H$ over $U$ as a section on the slice site, by restricting to each smaller open. It defines a morphism from the free module on one generator to $\mathcal H|_U$. Take its abelian image. The equivalence between the slice-site module category and modules on the open subscheme preserves kernels and cokernels and transports quasi-coherent presentations in both directions. Quasi-coherent kernel and cokernel closure therefore prove the image quasi-coherent. Push the single finite free generating section through the epimorphic image factorization; its local-generators data proves the image finite type. Evaluating the free-Hom equivalence at the unique generator shows that the original section belongs to the image on $U$.

Apply the finite-type submodule extension theorem with ambient sheaf $\mathcal H$ and prescribed submodule $\mathcal L\subseteq\mathcal H|_U$. Its hypotheses hold: $X$ is qcqs, $U$ is quasi-compact open, $\mathcal H$ is quasi-coherent, and $\mathcal L$ is quasi-coherent of finite type. Obtain a quasi-coherent finite-type $\mathcal K\subseteq\mathcal H$ with $\mathcal K|_U=\mathcal L$ as submodules. Composing with $\mathcal H\subseteq\mathcal G$ gives $\alpha_T(\mathcal K(T))=0$ on every open $T$, and $t\in\mathcal K(U)$.

Let $q:\mathcal G\to\mathcal Q$ be the cokernel of $\mathcal K\hookrightarrow\mathcal G$. The finite-type-source/finitely-presented-target cokernel theorem gives finite presentation of $\mathcal Q$. Since $\alpha$ vanishes on $\mathcal K$, the defining universal property of the cokernel supplies $\beta:\mathcal Q\to\mathcal F$ with $\beta q=\alpha$. Also $q_U(t)=0$ because $t\in\mathcal K(U)$ and $q$ kills the inclusion. Taking germs yields $q_x(s)=(q_U(t))_x=0$.
